title: How to Accept GCash Payments for Your Business in the Philippines
summary: Learn how Philippine businesses can accept GCash payments online and in-person — with QR Ph, payment links, and T+1 calendar day payouts in PHP.
body_markdown:

Sign up free with HitPay, verify with DTI or SEC and BIR documents, turn on GCash, then take it by link, QR or checkout. 2.3% online, 2% in person, T+1 payout.


## How to accept GCash as a business in the Philippines


1.


Sign up free at[hitpayapp.com/ph](https://hitpayapp.com/ph) . No setup or monthly fee.


2.


Verify your business: DTI registration (sole proprietors) or SEC registration (corporations and partnerships), BIR Form 2303, a valid government ID with a selfie check, and proof of your business bank account.


3.


Turn on GCash (and QR Ph) in your HitPay payment methods.


4.


Choose how customers pay: share a payment link in Messenger, Viber or email; show a QR code at the counter; or add GCash to your online checkout with the Shopify or WooCommerce plugin or the API.


5.


Get paid: GCash payouts reach your PHP bank account T+1 calendar day.

-


QR Ph: 1% or ₱20, whichever is higher


-


No setup fee and no monthly fee. Shopify orders add 0.5% for the Shopify app


-


Payouts: GCash, QR Ph and other non-card methods T+1 calendar day


-


HitPay is BSP registered


See[GCash on HitPay](https://hitpayapp.com/ph/gcash) for rates and setup.


The Philippine digital payments landscape has shifted decisively toward mobile wallets.[GCash](https://www.gcash.com/) has grown into one of the country’s dominant payment channels, and according to[World Bank financial inclusion](https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/financialinclusion) data, the Philippines has seen a marked expansion in digital financial services adoption as it works to bring more of its population into the formal financial system. For businesses in Makati, BGC, Cebu, or Davao, the operational question is no longer whether to accept GCash — it is how to do so efficiently, reliably, and at a cost structure that makes sense for an SME.


No website yet? You can send a[GCash payment link](https://hitpayapp.com/ph/payment-links) from HitPay and get paid in chat or by email.

Accepting GCash for a Philippine business? Online GCash is 2.3% and in-person GCash is 2%, with no monthly fee.

## What Does It Actually Mean to Accept GCash as a Business?


Accepting GCash as a business is distinct from simply using a personal GCash account to receive money. Consumer-to-consumer GCash transfers work for informal sellers, but they create reconciliation problems, lack proper transaction records, and do not scale.


Business-grade GCash acceptance means integrating GCash as a checkout payment method through a payment gateway or acquirer. When a customer pays via GCash at checkout — whether online or by scanning a QR code in-store — the transaction is processed through the gateway, recorded in the merchant’s dashboard, and settled to the merchant’s bank account in PHP.


Key operational differences from personal transfers:


-


Transactions are automatically reconciled and logged


-


Settlements go directly to a registered business bank account


-


Chargebacks and disputes are handled through a formal process


-


Transaction fees are clearly defined per payment


-


The[Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas](https://www.bsp.gov.ph/) requires that businesses processing electronic payments do so through a payment gateway — not through informal peer-to-peer transfers


## How Does GCash Work Within the QR Ph Ecosystem?


GCash payments in a business context almost always operate through QR Ph, the national QR code payment standard in the Philippines.[How to Generate QR Ph for Your Business](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/how-to-generate-qrph) explains the mechanics in detail, but the core principle is this: QR Ph is the interoperable standard that allows customers using GCash, Maya, or any QR Ph-compatible banking app to scan a single merchant QR code and complete payment from their preferred app.


This matters operationally. A merchant does not need a separate QR sticker for GCash and another for Maya. One QR Ph code handles both — and other participating bank apps. This interoperability is why QR Ph has become the standard for in-person cashless acceptance in Philippine retail, food service, and professional services.


For online payments, GCash operates as a wallet payment method at checkout — customers select GCash, authenticate in the GCash app, and the payment is confirmed in real time.


## What Are the Ways a Business Can Accept GCash?


There are four primary acceptance modes for GCash in a business context:


### Online Store Checkout


GCash is added as a payment option at checkout on an e-commerce store. When a customer selects GCash, they are redirected to complete authentication in the GCash app, then returned to the merchant’s confirmation page. This works with platforms including Shopify, WooCommerce, and Wix via payment gateway plugins. For online checkout integrations, see[HitPay’s payment gateway for the Philippines](https://hitpayapp.com/ph/payment-gateway) .


### Payment Links


Merchants generate a payment link and share it via Viber, Facebook Messenger, SMS, or email. The customer opens the link, selects GCash, and pays. No website is required. This is particularly practical for service businesses, freelancers, and sellers operating through social media. For businesses that also need to manage billing cycles,[Recurring Billing for Philippines Businesses](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/recurring-billing-ph) covers how to automate GCash-based subscription payments.


### Static QR Code


A static QR code is printed or displayed at the point of sale. Customers scan it with GCash or any QR Ph-compatible app. The amount is either pre-set or entered by the customer. This is the most common format for physical stores, market stalls, and food businesses across the Philippines.


### Soundbox / POS Terminal


[HitPay’s payment soundbox](https://hitpayapp.com/ph/payment-soundbox-philippines) displays a dynamic QR code for each transaction and plays an audio confirmation when payment is received — eliminating the need for staff to manually verify GCash notifications. This is operationally important for high-volume environments like cashier counters in Quezon City grocery stores or busy BGC food court stalls.

6.

## How Do GCash Settlements and Payouts Work?


Understanding payout timing is essential for cash flow management. For GCash transactions processed through HitPay in the Philippines:


-


**GCash, QR Ph and other non-card payments** : T+1 calendar day settlement in PHP


-


**Card payments** : online T+7 calendar days, in person T+2 calendar days


Funds settle to the merchant’s registered Philippine bank account. There is no minimum payout threshold requirement that delays settlement. Merchants can track transaction status and payout schedules in real time through the HitPay dashboard.


For transaction fee details, see hitpayapp.com/ph/pricing.


## Practical Takeaway


Accepting GCash as a Philippine business requires a payment gateway — not a personal wallet. The most operationally efficient setup combines GCash with QR Ph (for in-person interoperability), at least one alternative wallet (Maya, GrabPay), card acceptance, and a bank transfer option (InstaPay or PESONet) for customers who prefer direct bank payment. A static QR code handles walk-in traffic; payment links handle remote and social commerce sales. HitPay supports all of these within a single account, with no monthly fee and T+1 calendar day PHP settlement for GCash and other non-card payments.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can a business in Cebu or Davao (outside Metro Manila) accept GCash through HitPay?


Yes. HitPay operates across the Philippines and is not restricted to Metro Manila. Businesses in Cebu, Davao, or any other Philippine location can register, complete KYC remotely, and begin accepting GCash and[QR Ph payments](https://hitpayapp.com/ph/qr-ph) — online or in-person — without a physical onboarding requirement.


### Do Philippine businesses need a separate GCash merchant account to accept GCash?


No. When accepting GCash through a payment gateway like HitPay, merchants do not need to manage a separate GCash merchant account or GCash Business credentials directly. The payment gateway handles the integration with GCash on the merchant's behalf. Merchants simply enable GCash as a payment method within the HitPay dashboard and it becomes available at checkout.


### How much does HitPay charge to accept GCash?


2.3% per online GCash payment and 2% in person, excluding VAT. There's no setup or monthly fee. On a ₱1,000 online GCash payment, the fee is ₱23.


### How quickly does HitPay pay out GCash payments?


GCash payments are paid out to your PHP business bank account T+1 calendar day. Online card payments take T+7 and in-person card payments T+2 calendar days.


### What documents do I need to accept GCash through HitPay?


Sole proprietors need DTI registration; corporations and partnerships need SEC registration. Everyone needs BIR Form 2303, a valid government ID and proof of a business bank account.


### Is HitPay or PayMongo better for accepting GCash in the Philippines?


HitPay is better suited for Philippine SMEs that need multi-method acceptance (GCash, Maya, QR Ph, cards, BNPL, cross-border wallets) with zero monthly fees and T+1 calendar day PHP payouts for GCash. PayMongo positions itself toward fast-growing startups and developers seeking a fuller financial tools suite. Businesses that need tight integration with Philippine bank lending or capital products may find PayMongo's offering relevant; businesses prioritising breadth of payment methods and low fixed costs will find HitPay more appropriate.


### What is the difference between GCash and QR Ph for business payments?


GCash is a specific digital wallet operated by Globe, while QR Ph is the national interoperable QR payment standard in the Philippines, regulated by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. A merchant displaying a QR Ph code can receive payments from GCash users, Maya users, and any bank app that supports QR Ph — all from a single QR code. GCash-only acceptance, by contrast, excludes customers on other platforms. For in-person payments, QR Ph is the recommended standard precisely because of this interoperability.


### Can I accept GCash without a website in the Philippines?


Yes. Businesses without a website can accept GCash through payment links, which can be shared via Viber, Facebook Messenger, SMS, or email. The customer opens the link, selects GCash, and completes payment. HitPay's payment link feature supports GCash and does not require any e-commerce platform or technical integration.


### How do I accept GCash payments for my business in the Philippines?


Businesses in the Philippines accept GCash by connecting a payment gateway that supports GCash as a checkout method. HitPay supports GCash acceptance for online stores, payment links, and in-person QR Ph transactions. The process involves registering a HitPay account, passing KYC verification, and enabling GCash in the payment methods dashboard. No monthly fees apply — merchants pay a per-transaction fee only.
